title: Gerund vs Infinitive Nuances
summary: Choose between gerunds, infinitives, and verbal periphrases to express progress, manner, purpose, and sequence.

sections.heading: Gerund for manner and simultaneous action
sections.body: Beyond estar + gerúndio, the gerund can show how something happens or that two actions happen at the same time. In standard writing, avoid using it to replace every subordinate clause.

examples.en: I learned Portuguese by listening to podcasts.

examples.pt: Ele respondeu olhando para o chão.
examples.en: He answered while looking at the floor.

sections.heading: Infinitive for purpose and after prepositions
sections.body: The infinitive often expresses purpose after **para** and follows many prepositions and verbs. It can be personal when it has its own subject.

examples.en: I left early to avoid traffic.

examples.pt: Antes de sair, apague as luzes.
examples.en: Before leaving, turn off the lights.

examples.pt: Para eles entenderem, precisamos dar exemplos.
examples.en: For them to understand, we need to give examples.

sections.heading: Brazilian sensitivity to gerundismo
sections.body: Brazilian Portuguese uses gerunds naturally, but excessive bureaucratic chains like **vou estar verificando** are criticized as **gerundismo** when a simpler form works.

examples.en: I will be checking your request.
I am checking your request now.

keyPoints: Gerunds can show simultaneous action or manner.
Infinitives commonly express purpose after para.
Personal infinitive appears when the infinitive has its own subject.
Avoid unnecessary gerundismo in formal or professional communication.

commonMistakes.note: Avoid gerundismo when simple future works.
